question: The fragments of Okazaki are:

options.opa: The result of the proteolysis of DNA polymerase.
options.opb: DNA fragments that are sintered in the 3'-> 5 direction.
options.opc: Fragments of RNA that act as primers.
options.opd: Fragments of DNA in the delayed strand.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "DNA replication" -> "lagging strand synthesis" -> "discontinuous synthesis" -> "Okazaki fragments" -> 90%
CHAIN: "DNA polymerase" -> "synthesizes DNA" -> "5' to 3' direction" -> "Okazaki fragments on lagging strand" -> 90%
CHAIN: "RNA primers" -> "initiate DNA synthesis" -> "Okazaki fragments" -> "joined by DNA ligase" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Lagging strand" -> "synthesized in short segments" -> "Okazaki fragments" -> "joined to form continuous strand" -> 90%
CHAIN: "DNA replication" -> "leading strand continuous" -> "lagging strand discontinuous" -> "Okazaki fragments" -> 90%
analysis: Okazaki fragments are short sequences of DNA nucleotides which are synthesized discontinuously and later linked together by the enzyme DNA ligase to create the lagging strand during DNA replication. These fragments are formed on the lagging strand because DNA polymerase can only synthesize DNA in the 5' to 3' direction, necessitating the synthesis of short segments that are later joined together.
